= Limitations

This is a rough-and-ready list of current-state features, planned features, and
non-features.

== Language Features in a Non-Working State

* Section IDs are generated by the Asciidoctor-style HTML backend (`_my_section`,
  just as Asciidoctor does), but not by the HTMLBook backend, and they are not
  part of the parsed document (the `json` output), so a cross reference to a
  generated ID (`+<<_my_section>>+`) links correctly, but shows the ID rather
  than the section title, and logs a warning
* Custom text for cross references: `+<<id,custom text>>+` is left as text
  (`+<<id>>+` works, and uses the title of the target)
* Nested lists (`** nested`) are not recognized
* List continuations (`+`) inside lists are unreliable; a continuation that
  attaches a nested list, for example, will garble the list
* A list item with a continuation garbles the list if another item follows it:
  `* one`, `+`, `more`, `* two` merges "more" into the first item's text
  ("onemore"), leaves the second item empty, and moves "two" out of the list
  into a paragraph before it. A continuation on the last item of a list works
* A footnote in a list item moves the item's text out of the item's principal
  text if an earlier footnote exists in the document
* `+pass:[]+` inline passthroughs work, but `+++text+++` does not (it is
  treated as a code span), and `[pass]` is not recognized as a paragraph style
* Typographic replacements are not complete: ` -- ` becomes a plain em dash
  (Asciidoctor adds thin spaces around it), and apostrophes inside some spans
  (e.g., `+_don't_+`) are not replaced
* An ID on an admonition (`[[id]]` above `NOTE: text`) ends up on the content of
  the admonition, not on the admonition itself

== Working Caveats

Tables:: Tables are rendered as expected, save that `asciidocr` does not
currently respect column width designations; `cols="3,1,1"` will still produce a
three-column table, but with columns of "default" widths. Tables also do not
currently support spanning columns or rows; if you require this functionality,
please use an HTML table in a passthrough block.

Block titles:: Titles on listing, literal and verse blocks, tables,
admonitions, examples, sidebars and images are rendered. Titles on passthrough
blocks are parsed but not rendered.

Titles on lists:: A block title above a list (`.Title` then `* item`) is
parsed and kept in the ASG, and is rendered by the Asciidoctor-style HTML
backend. It is intentionally not rendered by the HTMLBook backend (or the DOCX
backend) yet; the HTMLBook backend logs a warning instead.

Titles on paragraphs:: Not supported, and not planned. The paragraph is kept,
and the title is dropped with a warning.

Special characters:: Text and attribute values are escaped in the HTML backends
(`&`, `<` and `>`, plus quotation marks in attributes), except that character
references (`&amp;`, `&#8217;`, etc.) are left as they are, as in Asciidoctor,
and passthroughs are output exactly as written. Unlike Asciidoctor, quote and
verse attributions are escaped too.

== Asciidoctor-style HTML backend

The Asciidoctor-style backend (`-b asciidoctor`) produces the markup and
classes Asciidoctor produces (checked against Asciidoctor 2.0.17), without its
stylesheet. Known gaps:

* Callout lists
* Table column widths are always shared out evenly, and table cell alignment and
  styles are not supported
* A `[source]` block without a language is rendered like any other listing
  (as `<pre>`, not `<pre class="highlight"><code>`)
* Checklists and admonition icons

== Language Features Planned for Inclusion Later

* https://docs.asciidoctor.org/asciidoc/latest/attributes/positional-and-named-attributes/#block-style-and-attribute-shorthand[block style
attribute short hand] -- I'm both not a fan (just use `role=` and `[[id]]`, etc.!) and parsing this is going to be semi-annoying so I shall put it off.
* Hardbreaks-option attribute (which we shall include for our poet friends who
  don't want to have to wrap everything in `[verse]`) 
* https://docs.asciidoctor.org/asciidoc/latest/document/author-information/[Author information]
* https://docs.asciidoctor.org/asciidoc/latest/document/revision-information/[Revision information]
* https://docs.asciidoctor.org/asciidoc/latest/document/metadata/[Document metadata]
* https://docs.asciidoctor.org/asciidoc/latest/document/doctype/[Document types]
* https://docs.asciidoctor.org/asciidoc/latest/sections/section-ref/[Section
  Attributes and styles]
* Paragraph alignment and indented blocks 
* Substitutions (quote substitutions now working!)
* Checklists
* Autolinks for emails (http:: urls now work!)
* `mailto:`
* `Footnote:id` syntax (this may not happen)
* Icons
* Keyboard/button/etc. macros (I mean to target "writers," first, then
  "technical writers" at some later point).
* Syntax highlighting for source blocks
* STEM and equations
* Automatic Tables of Contents
* Deeply nested description lists (in the meantime: just use an open block)
* Discrete Headings

== Language Features Not Currently Planned for Inclusion

https://docs.asciidoctor.org/asciidoc/latest/macros/audio-and-video/[Audio and
video]:: Maybe… later? Not part of the current project target(s), which are more
document-focused.

https://docs.asciidoctor.org/asciidoc/latest/macros/footnote/#externalizing-a-footnote[Externalized
footnotes]:: I think that it's clearer to include footnote text where it ought
to go (and don't really believe there are many great footnote reuse use-cases);
Supporting this would require a second-pass on the attribute parsing, which
we're not really doing at the moment. Can be added later, but no plans
currently.

https://docs.asciidoctor.org/asciidoc/latest/attributes/counters/[Counters]::
Given that these are a "poorly defined feature in Asciidoc," and I've never,
myself, found a use for them, there are no plans for support.

https://docs.asciidoctor.org/asciidoc/latest/directives/conditionals/[Conditionals]::
This probably wouldn't be too hard to implement, but (selfishly) I've yet to
find a need for these, so have no current plans for supporting them. If this is
of interest, open an issue.

https://docs.asciidoctor.org/asciidoc/latest/blocks/collapsible/[Collapsible
blocks]:: Again, this feels a more web-oriented feature; at least for the
moment, we're targeting document creation.

== Limitations of the DOCX Backend

The DOCX backend is experimental.

* List continuations
* Titles on lists
* Headers on tables
* Footnotes are included in-line and highlighted, not as footnotes
* Only checked in LibreOffice so far (not in Word)
